identity.description: Slack is a workspace messaging and collaboration platform (slack.com). Slack's developer platform, documented at docs.slack.dev, exposes the Web API, Events API, Socket Mode, Incoming Webhooks, and an official Slack-hosted MCP server.
identity.identity_notes: Sources clearly describe the Slack workspace messaging product and its developer platform. Slack's own docs, the official slackapi GitHub org, and Slack's help center all point to the same product.

auth.oauth_flows: OAuth 2.0 v2 install flow: the app exchanges a code via oauth.v2.access for bot or user tokens. For MCP, Slack supports confidential OAuth with client_id/client_secret, user authorize endpoint https://slack.com/oauth/v2_user/authorize, token endpoint https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.user.access; PKCE for desktop clients. DCR and SSE are not supported.
auth.token_refresh: unknown: sources do not describe refresh-token behavior for bot or user tokens. Workflow tokens expire after 15 minutes.
auth.scopes_notes: Granular OAuth scopes, especially for bot users (v2 flow). Bot tokens (xoxb-) are tied to an installed app; user tokens (xoxp-) are issued to the installing user and authenticating users. App-level tokens (xapp-) are used for Socket Mode. Workflow tokens (xwfp-) expire after 15 minutes. Service tokens are only for Deno Slack SDK apps.

access.production_restrictions: For the MCP server only: Only apps published in the Slack Marketplace and internal apps can use MCP at this time; workspace admins must approve MCP client integrations. Unlisted apps are not permitted. Marketplace listing requires Slack's standard app approval process. The Web API has no stated production review in these sources.

resources: Slack MCP server (JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP)
read_ops: search messages, files, users, channels, emoji (MCP)
write_ops: create and update lists and records
api.rate_limits: Tiered per method: Tier 2 (20+/min) to Tier 4 (100+/min); search and message-sending have special limits (per Slack MCP docs).
api.limitations: Web API is HTTP RPC-style and Slack says it is 'not a REST API'; REST is the closest enum value. Method count is stated as 'over 200' on the Web API page and 'over 270' in the Node SDK README. The MCP server only works with Marketplace-published or internal apps and does not support SSE or Dynamic Client Registration. Events API is delivered via Socket Mode or HTTP request URL.
